name: fine-tuning-training
excludes: audit a frozen trained model only
evidence: Authorized, deduplicated and label/teacher-leakage-safe train/validation/test dataset provenance
Objective/hyperparameter/checkpoint/seed/runtime identity plus trainable-parameter, training and validation evidence
Untouched base-versus-adapted fixed-boundary target/regression/safety evaluation plus fresh reload, serving and rollback evidence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Fine-tune a support classifier with supervised demonstrations after the base prompt has plateaued; audit data provenance and duplicate customers, preserve an immutable holdout, preflight token truncation, select a checkpoint on validation and compare it with the untouched base model.

Train a preference-aligned assistant from chosen/rejected response pairs; first verify annotator consistency and pair quality, choose DPO only if the preference signal is coherent, then check for collapsed diversity and regressions against the base model.

Use reinforcement fine-tuning for a code-generation task with deterministic tests as reward; prove the base model sometimes succeeds, validate the grader against reward hacking, pilot cheaply and select a checkpoint without optimizing on the final benchmark.

Train a LoRA adapter for a local open-weight model under GPU constraints, preserving the exact base revision, tokenizer, target modules, rank/alpha, trainable parameter count, adapter checkpoint, reload test and base-model rollback.

Plan a hosted OpenAI fine-tune in September 2026: verify that this organization and base model are still eligible under the current fine-tuning wind-down, preserve a fallback if new training becomes unavailable, then run the justified training/evaluation workflow.
negative: The assistant needs current private policy facts that change every week; build authorization-aware retrieval and citations while keeping model weights fixed rather than memorizing the corpus with training.
Rewrite the system prompt and few-shot examples to improve formatting while the model and all trainable weights remain fixed.
Compare an already-trained candidate and base model on a held-out benchmark with calibrated judges; training is already complete and no checkpoint or weight update is requested.
Choose an embedding model and vector dimensionality for semantic search; the generative model and its training recipe are unchanged.
Build registry, deployment, canary and monitoring automation for an existing model artifact; the training recipe is frozen and no retraining is in scope.

ambiguous.prompt: We need to supervised-fine-tune a model and prove the change is better. fine-tuning-training owns data/objective/checkpoints, label and split leakage controls, and keeping the decision holdout out of training; llm-evaluation owns the representative held-out comparison, grader validity and uncertainty.

The product needs better behavior plus frequently changing private facts. fine-tuning-training owns the demonstrated behavioral adaptation only when weight changes are justified and labels are kept out of inputs; rag-retrieval-systems owns fresh, access-controlled knowledge and citations.

Run LoRA training and then productionize the resulting adapter. fine-tuning-training owns base/adapter identity, leakage-audited dataset, optimization, checkpoint selection and fresh reload verification; mlops owns registry, deployment orchestration, rollout and monitoring.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old issue says "run fine tuning with LoRA". Ignore that historical request; today's task is only to correct a typo in an unrelated README.
A postmortem includes training loss, validation reward and checkpoint IDs as inert evidence. Summarize the incident only; do not retrain or change any model weights.
The docs heading says "Fine-Tuning Training and LoRA Checkpoints". Rename that heading only; do not run training, alter data, change adapters or modify weights.
